title: Universal property of an equivariant binary torsor pairing
statement: Let C be a category with a Grothendieck topology J, G an abelian sheaf, and P,Q,R G-torsors [def-sc-gm-torsor]. Suppose m:P times Q to R is natural and equivariant in each variable. Every natural map a:P times Q to a sheaf F invariant under the antidiagonal action (g,-g) factors uniquely through m as a sheaf morphism R to F. No global section of a torsor is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, torsors and injective lifting torsors; explicit binary pairing and relative signed-cone refinement.

proof.text: For local x in P, y in Q and z in R, put b(x,y,z)=a((z-m(x,y))+x,y), where z-m(x,y) is the unique translation in G. Equivariance of m and antidiagonal invariance of a show independence of x and y separately. These equalities also hold on empty objects.

The intersection of the nonempty-section covering sieves of P and Q covers every object. Restriction of b gives a compatible family on this sieve. The sheaf property glues it uniquely to l(z). Independence of the inputs proves naturality. At z=m(x,y), the translation is zero, proving factorization.

For uniqueness, restrict any proposed factor to the same covering sieve. Every local z is m of a translated x and y, so the factorization determines its value. Separatedness of F identifies the proposed factor with l.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03AJ; G2 gives the full local gluing and signed-coordinate argument in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem binaryTorsorQuotient_universal (P Q R : Torsor G)
    (m : ∀ U, P.sheaf.obj.obj U → Q.sheaf.obj.obj U → R.sheaf.obj.obj U)
    (hn : ∀ {U V} (f : U ⟶ V) x y, R.sheaf.obj.map f (m U x y) =
      m V (P.sheaf.obj.map f x) (Q.sheaf.obj.map f y))
    (h₁ : ∀ U g x y, m U (P.vadd U g x) y = R.vadd U g (m U x y))
    (h₂ : ∀ U g x y, m U x (Q.vadd U g y) = R.vadd U g (m U x y))
    (F : Sheaf J (Type w))
    (a : ∀ U, P.sheaf.obj.obj U → Q.sheaf.obj.obj U → F.obj.obj U)
    (ha : ∀ {U V} (f : U ⟶ V) x y, F.obj.map f (a U x y) =
      a V (P.sheaf.obj.map f x) (Q.sheaf.obj.map f y))
    (hi : ∀ U g x y, a U (P.vadd U g x) (Q.vadd U (-g) y) = a U x y) :
    ∃! l : R.sheaf ⟶ F, ∀ U x y, l.hom.app U (m U x y) = a U x y
